description: roti bakar — toast in Southeast Asia commonly served with butter and kaya, dipped in softboiled eggs. the word roti is Malay for bread, and bakar means "burned", alluding to the challenge i've chosen to tackle, which is hot spots!
summary: SO FIRE is an interactive web application to monitor, analyse, and visualise global wildfire dynamics with sub-daily precision. For this initial release, the dataset scope is intentionally bounded to August 2026 because it captures the peak dry season and agricultural burning cycle driving the severe transboundary haze crisis in Southeast Asia, which is the region I'm from. Utilising a custom normalisation pipeline and an optimised HTML5 Canvas density renderer, the platform allows researchers, emergency responders, and the public to explore fire radiative power (FRP) and hotspot clusters across custom Areas of Interest (AOIs). While currently optimised around this critical August 2026 baseline for immediate regional impact and high-resolution analysis, the underlying architecture is fully built for future expansion to global, multi-year climate archives.
details:
What It Does & How It Works

  • Targeted Temporal Baseline: Focused exclusively on the August 2026 sharded daily datasets. This specific month was chosen to tackle the acute, recurring threat of the Southeast Asian transboundary haze crisis, providing high-resolution data on smoke-producing peat and agricultural fires affecting local air quality.
  • Future Expansion Roadmap: Designed with a modular data pipeline that allows the current single-month framework to scale effortlessly toward multi-year historical archives, real-time satellite telemetry ingestion, and global expansion to other high-risk fire regions worldwide.
  • High-Performance Canvas Rendering: Employs an HTML5 Canvas-based density layer to smoothly render thousands of wildfire data points in real time without browser lag.
  • Custom Data Architecture: Leverages a sharded .json.gz data model coupled with a custom preprocessing pipeline (requirements.txt, python pipeline scripts) to lightweight-stream daily global fire records.
  • Area of Interest (AOI) Tools: Features interactive drawing tools allowing users to define custom bounding boxes or coordinate points to filter and analyse local fire statistics instantly.
  • Dual Metric Modes: Switches dynamically between raw fire counts and Fire Radiative Power (FRP) to distinguish between routine agricultural clearing and catastrophic, high-energy blazes.

Benefits & Intended Impact

  • Haze Mitigation & Early Warning: Directly targets regional smoke pollution by isolating high-FRP clusters in vulnerable tropical ecosystems, giving authorities actionable lead time before plumes cross international borders.
  • Instant Accessibility: Runs entirely client-side via GitHub Pages, removing the need for heavy GIS software installations or expensive server-side mapping backends.
  • Scalable Framework: Designed to handle multi-gigabyte satellite observation records through optimised file sharding, making complex climate and atmospheric data easily digestible for local stakeholders.

Tools, Languages, & Software Used

  • Frontend: HTML5, CSS3, JavaScript (ES6 Modules)
  • Mapping & Graphics: Leaflet.js, HTML5 Canvas API, CARTO vector/raster tile services
  • Data Processing & Pipeline: Python, gzip compression models, GeoJSON
  • Deployment & Version Control: Git, GitHub Pages, GitHub Actions

Creativity & Key Considerations

  • Personal & Regional Relevance: Grounding the application in the August 2026 window bridges raw satellite telemetry with an urgent, lived geopolitical issue: the Southeast Asian haze, making the tool immediately meaningful to regional environmental protection.
  • Performance Optimisation: Overcame the challenge of rendering heavy geospatial datasets in a web browser by implementing custom spatial binning and logarithmic color scaling via an explicit lookup table (LUT).
